root_idea.summary: The root centers on securing something and keeping it preserved.
root_idea.development: This develops into storing, hoarding, reserving, and preparing provisions for future need. The lexical family also extends to bodily spaces conceived as receptacles; the plant name إِذْخِرٌ is explicitly treated as unrelated to this semantic root.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Presented under the normalized Classical Arabic perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To store, hoard, or lay something up for future need.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrence describes keeping something stored in one's house. The derived verb may also frame such storage as preparation for what lies ahead, including preparation for the hereafter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To choose or select something and take it for oneself, or prepare it for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical extension of the basic act of laying something up or securing it for personal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reserve or preserve something for oneself, including a good story or good advice retained inwardly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative examples extend the idea of laying something up to remembered speech and inwardly retained counsel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A store, treasure, or provision laid up for future need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal designation for something secured and kept in reserve.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stored reserve, treasured provision, or thing laid up for need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is also used figuratively of wealth devoted to pious purposes and of believers' deeds laid up as provision for the Day of Resurrection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fat or corpulent, used as an epithet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare adjectival or epithet use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet-smelling rush or herb, identified with plants such as juncus odoratus or schoenanthum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant is used for roofing and graves and as an ingredient in perfumes; it is lexically distinguished from the storage root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The inner parts of the body, especially the intestines, lower belly, veins, or the bodily parts in which an animal stores fodder and water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَذَاخِرُ is used in expressions where filling these parts means becoming satiated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a figurative idiom, the heart or inner seat that can be filled with enmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is attested in the expression مَلَأَ فِي مَذَاخِرِهِ عَدَاوَةً, 'he filled his heart with enmity.'

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that reserves some of its running power for a time of need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine description; the related variant مُذَّخِرٌ is also recorded.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers storage, preparation, selection, and the related verbal-noun designation.
Figurative reservation or preservation for oneself.
Retaining advice inwardly is covered by the figurative retention meaning.
Defines ذَخِيرَةٌ as a stored reserve or provision.
Spiritual application of a reserve to wealth devoted to pious use.
Spiritual application to deeds stored as provision for resurrection.
Rare epithet meaning fat or corpulent.
Plant name and its described uses.
Contains both the anatomical meaning and the figurative enmity idiom.

cautions: The single QAC occurrence is an imperfect Form VIII verb; the public headword is normalized to the perfect citation form اِدَّخَرَ.
إِذْخِرٌ, the fragrant plant name, is explicitly distinguished from the storage-related root despite its similar spelling.
